title: Intelligent prefill+decode routing playbook for speculative decoding
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a pragmatic runtime playbook and reference implementation that enables low-latency speculative decoding with deterministic acceptance metrics and deterministic graceful fallback. This ticket captures design choices, acceptance thresholds, fallback strategies, and a minimal runtime shim to evaluate effectiveness across representative workloads.

Scope: implement routing decisions that pick a candidate fast-path model (or kernel variant) for prefill and an associated decode path; compute an acceptance score by combining early-token confidence, kernel-compatibility signals, and a lightweight quality proxy; implement a deterministic rollback/fallback when acceptance falls below threshold; wire telemetry and controlled rollout knobs in Console. Excludes: long-term autoscaler changes and persistent prefix cache redesign (separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime can select and attempt a speculative fast-path for at least 3 model+kernel pairings and record selection reasons in trace.
2) An acceptance metric computed within 5ms of first decode token is emitted (confidence_percent, kernel_affinity_score, combined_acceptance_score).
3) When acceptance_score < threshold, runtime automatically switches to fallback decode path within the same request and emits fallback event.
4) End-to-end 95th percentile latency for the speculative+fallback flow does not regress more than 10% compared to non-speculative baseline on target test fleet.
5) Console exposes per-route acceptance rate, fallback rate, and cost delta for rollout monitoring.
design_decisions:
- Use a two-stage routing decision: (A) prefill sampler selects candidate model variant + kernel based on historical per-route cost/latency and a small stochastic component; (B) early-decode probe (first N tokens or KV-sample) yields a fast acceptance signal.
- Acceptance metric is a weighted sum: early_token_confidence (softmax-based proxy), kernel_fingerprint_match (binary/score), runtime_resource_headroom (normalized). Weights tunable via Console.
- Fallback semantics: do not return partial output from failed speculative decode. Instead, abort the speculative decode and resume on the fallback model while preserving client-visible continuity via a short-lived stream stall and a metric that labels the operation as speculative-fallback.
- Kernel selection favors quantized, attention-optimized kernels for short-sequence fast-paths; fallback uses full-precision or alternate GEMM kernels depending on compatibility.
- Safety: all routing decisions are deterministic given the same routing inputs to make debugging and replays feasible. Metrics include random-seed used for stochastic selection.
- Opt for runtime-side accept/retry rather than client retry to avoid duplicating tokens upstream and to simplify client semantics.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (lab): implement shim and unit tests; verify acceptance metric matches offline simulation on 10k prompts.
Phase 1 (canary): enable on 1% of traffic for low-latency routes; monitor acceptance_rate, fallback_rate, cost_change, and runtime errors for 72h.
Phase 2 (ramp): increase to 10% if canary metrics look good; run A/B against non-speculative baseline for quality delta.
Phase 3 (opt-in): expose route-level toggle in Console with per-route thresholds and kernel preferences.
Rollback: global kill-switch in control-plane to short-circuit speculative path; immediate 0% rollout if fallback_rate > 5% or customer_error_rate increases by > 0.2%.
telemetry_and_metrics:
Emit the following per-request events: routing_decision: {candidate_id,kernel_tag,reason_scores}, early_acceptance: {confidence,affinity,combined_score}, fallback_event: {fallback_target,latency_penalty,reason}, final_outcome: {accepted|fallback|error}.
Aggregate dashboards: acceptance_rate (per-model, per-route), fallback_rate, mean/95/99 latency delta vs baseline, token-cost delta, CPU/GPU utilization delta for kernel variants.
Instrument synthetic prompt sets (short, medium, long) for continuous quality regression checks.
Retention: keep traces for 30 days for debugging; sample 1% of successful speculative paths for full trace recording.
tests_and_qa:
Unit tests for acceptance score computation covering edge cases (zero-confidence, kernel-mismatch).
Integration tests: simulated abort+fallback preserving KV cache semantics, verify no token duplication, and validate streaming behavior when fallback occurs mid-stream.
Load test: synthetic 10k qps workload with mixed prompt lengths; verify latency SLOs and fallback contention.
Canary checklist: smoke-test generator correctness, validate metric emission, and manual inspection of 50 sampled traces for content-quality regressions.
Post-release: run an offline A/B eval suite comparing top-1 completion quality between speculative accepted and fallback samples.
implementation_notes:
- Add RoutingShim proto: flattened routing inputs (route_id, model_catalog_score, kernel_profile, resource_headroom, rand_seed). Keep proto versioned.
- Implement FastProbe module to run lightweight early-token scoring without touching large attention contexts where possible (uses a cached shallow attention pass).
- Integrate with kernel selector: allow 'trial' binding where we mark candidate kernel and can abort if hardware mismatch occurs.
- Ensure decode scheduler supports early abort and resume semantics: decode must be cancellable and handoffable to fallback decoder without leaking KV state.
- Add Console toggles and rollout config keys: speculative_enabled, acceptance_threshold, kernel_preference_list, fallback_policy.
- Backfill e2e tests in GH: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/ TBD.
- Estimate: 2 weeks core runtime + 1 week telemetry + 1 week testing and canary support (estimate already recorded above).
